newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seeks to join World Health Organisation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seeks to join World Health Organisation.

text.p: Taiwan said on Wednesday it had applied to become an observer at the U.N. World Health Organisation (WHO) and urged rival China not to block its bid.

Foreign Minister John Chang told a news conference he sent the island's application to the WHO's director-general Hiroshi Nakajima on April 3 and the organisation was expected to give a ruling during its annual meeting in May.
Chang said Taiwan decided to take part in the WHO because it was the least politically sensitive body of all U.N. organisations.
"Mainland China should not adopt its usual stubborn ideology to oppress and obstruct our application," Chang said. "Such action will only increase hostility of our countrymen towards the mainland."
China has regarded Taiwan as a rebel-held province ineligible for international recognition since a civil war split them in 1949.
Beijing, which took China's U.N. seat from Taipei in 1971, has blocked Taipei's membership as a sovereign state in all international forums.

Taiwan, which has insisted the island's 21 million people deserve a voice in the United Nations, has launched bids to join the world body since 1993. Its attempts were defeated for four consecutive years by China and its supporters.
Chang reiterated the island's desire to join the United Nations, but said U.N. membership would be a long-term goal.
